name: Tiller & Persinger 2002: time-reversed Thomas pattern, right (5 min)
summary: The 849-point 'Thomas' table played backwards (pulses speeding up instead of slowing down), at 3 ms per point mainly over the right parietotemporal region for 5 min: the comparison block that Tiller & Persinger 2002 reported as less effective than the forward pattern for left-sided presences. In the study it always came straight after the forward block.
notes: 12 subjects got eight 5-min blocks in one fixed order, 'primarily over the right parietotemporal region', through a helmet with four pairs of solenoids, each pair on for 5 s (20 s per rotation). The reversed pattern at 3 ms was block 6, always straight after the forward 3-ms block, so pattern and order cannot be told apart (Tiller 2002 p.1-2 [26-27]). This program plays the forward table (849 values of Table 1 of US 6,234,953) in reverse point order, at 3 ms per point with a 3-ms pause between repeats, and the left side at a fifth of the right. The pause and the fifth are from the helmet paper (Persinger 2000 p.3 [661]); this paper gives neither. Buckner 2015 p.2 says only that the reverse file 'proceeds from 6 Hz to 25 Hz'; whether the lab reversed every point, as here, or only the order of the pulses is not stated. One left-right pair is on at a time (5 s each), and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. Field: 'approximately 1 microTesla (10 milligauss)' averaged over the scalp (p.2 [27]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT this helmet's field model gives a peak of about 24 uT at the scalp, over ten times the paper's average. 12 people, one lab; the difference between forward and reversed has never been repeated. persinger-tiller-2002-thomas-right is the forward block. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop at once on fear, headache or distress.
setting: Blindfolded or with opaque goggles in a quiet, dark room; report the moment and side of anything felt.
schedule: One 5-min block, at most once a week.
source: Tiller & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:26 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11883572/ ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (849 points at 3 ms, 2.55-s cycle) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Murugan 2013, thesis, Laurentian University, pp. 44-45 (248-point burst-x, 849-point Thomas pulse, 3-ms points) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/39c9c1ad-70ba-458d-a819-d24c20da217a ; Persinger & Belanger-Chellew 1999, Percept Mot Skills 89:486 (3-ms pixel and interstimulus optimum in rats) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10597585/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
